    Proposition 2.6(3): k(Γ_A) is the radical grading of ind(mod A) #

    The source paper. Sending each arrow to its chosen class in C_1 = Irr defines a functor from the path category; it kills each mesh relation, because the degree-two part of p ∘ i = 0 is the image of r_Y; the resulting graded functor k(Γ_A) → gr_J ind(mod A) is surjective because the radical layers are generated in degree one, and injective by induction on the degree, using the exactness of Proposition 2.6(1).

    Formally, choose for each arrow a : x → y a representative rep a ∈ J(x, y) of the chosen basis vector of Irr(x, y). A path is realized by the composite of the representatives (pathMap), and a morphism of kQ by linear extension (realize). A path of length d lands in J^d, so a homogeneous morphism of degree d has a class in the radical layer J^d/J^{d+1}.
